q.t: A transversal cuts two parallel lines. The corresponding angles are:
q.e: Parallel lines point in the same direction, so the transversal leans against each of them at the same angle.

q.t: A transversal cuts two parallel lines. The alternate interior angles are:
q.e: They form a Z shape. Each equals the same corresponding angle (via vertically opposite angles), so they equal each other.

q.t: A transversal cuts two parallel lines. The interior angles on the same side of the transversal add up to:
q.e: One of them plus the linear-pair partner of the other are corresponding (equal), so the two together make a straight angle: 180°.

q.t: A line that cuts two or more lines at different points is called a:
q.e: ‘Transversal’ means lying across — it crosses the other lines.

q.t: Lines are parallel and one of a pair of corresponding angles is 70°. Find the other (in degrees).
q.e: Corresponding angles on parallel lines are equal.

q.t: Lines are parallel and one of a pair of alternate interior angles is 55°. Find the other (in degrees).
q.e: Alternate interior angles on parallel lines are equal.

q.t: Lines are parallel and one of a pair of co-interior angles is 110°. Find the other (in degrees).
q.e: Co-interior angles (same side, between the lines) add to 180°: 180 − 110 = 70.

q.t: Two parallel lines in a plane meet at:
q.e: Parallel lines stay the same distance apart for ever, so they never meet.

q.t: A transversal crosses two lines. How many angles are formed in all?
q.e: Four angles at each crossing point, and there are two crossing points: 4 + 4 = 8.

q.t: Two different lines in a plane are both perpendicular to the same line. They are:
q.e: Both make 90° with the third line — equal corresponding angles — so they must be parallel.

q.t: Co-interior angles on parallel lines are 2x° and 3x°. Find the larger angle (in degrees).
q.e: They add to 180: 5x = 180, x = 36. Larger = 108.

q.t: Alternate interior angles on parallel lines are (3x − 10)° and (2x + 15)°. Find x.
q.e: Alternate angles are equal: 3x − 10 = 2x + 15, so x = 25.

q.t: Corresponding angles on parallel lines are 5x° and (3x + 40)°. Find each angle (in degrees).
q.e: Equal: 5x = 3x + 40, x = 20. Each angle = 100.

q.t: A transversal (not perpendicular) cuts two parallel lines and one angle is 65°. How many of the 8 angles are 65°?
q.e: At each crossing two angles are 65° (vertically opposite) and two are 115°. The same pattern repeats on the second line: 4 angles of 65°.

q.t: Co-interior angles on parallel lines are (x + 20)° and (2x − 50)°. Find x.
q.e: They add to 180: 3x − 30 = 180, so x = 70. (Angles 90° and 90°.)

q.t: On parallel lines, one co-interior angle is 4 times the other. Find the smaller (in degrees).
If line l is parallel to m, and m is parallel to n, then:
o: l meets n at one point
q.e: All three point in the same direction, so l and n never meet either.

q.t: A transversal cuts two parallel lines. The alternate exterior angles are:
q.e: Each is vertically opposite to one of a pair of alternate interior angles, which are equal.

q.t: A transversal is perpendicular to one of two parallel lines. What angle does it make with the other (in degrees)?
q.e: The corresponding angle on the second line equals the 90° on the first.

q.t: On parallel lines, one interior angle is 75°. Find the interior angle on the same side of the transversal (in degrees).
q.e: Same-side interior angles add to 180°: 180 − 75 = 105.

q.t: AB ∥ CD and E is a point between the two lines. ∠ABE = 40° and ∠CDE = 30° (both measured between the parallels). Find ∠BED (in degrees).
q.e: Draw a line through E parallel to AB and CD. It splits ∠BED into two parts that are alternate to 40° and 30°, so ∠BED = 70°.

q.t: Co-interior angles on parallel lines differ by 40°. Find the larger (in degrees).
A transversal makes corresponding angles of 72° and 78° with two lines. The lines are:
q.e: Corresponding angles are equal ONLY when lines are parallel. 72 ≠ 78, so these lines will meet somewhere.

q.t: Alternate interior angles on parallel lines are (x/2 + 30)° and (x − 10)°. Find x.
Co-interior angles on parallel lines are in the ratio 5 : 4. Find the smaller (in degrees).
q.e: 9 parts make 180°, so one part is 20°. Smaller = 80.

q.t: In △ABC, a line through A is drawn parallel to BC. ∠B = 50° and ∠C = 60°. The two angles this line makes with AB and AC (outside the triangle) are:
q.e: They are alternate to ∠B and ∠C, so they equal 50° and 60°. Together with ∠A they make a straight line — which is why a triangle’s angles add to 180°.

q.t: A transversal cuts two parallel lines. The bisectors of a pair of co-interior angles meet at an angle of:
q.e: The co-interior angles add to 180°, so their halves add to 90°. In the triangle the bisectors form, the third angle is 180 − 90 = 90°.

q.t: Co-interior angles on parallel lines are (3x + 15)° and (2x + 5)°. Find x.
Corresponding angles on parallel lines are (4x − 12)° and (2x + 48)°. Find each angle (in degrees).
AB ∥ CD and E is a point between the lines. ∠ABE = 130° and ∠CDE = 140°. Find ∠BED (in degrees).
q.e: Draw a line through E parallel to AB. Co-interior angles give the two parts of ∠BED as 180 − 130 = 50 and 180 − 140 = 40. Total 90°.

q.t: AB ∥ CD and E is a point between the lines. ∠ABE = 35° and ∠BED = 80°. Find ∠CDE (in degrees).
q.e: With a line through E parallel to both, ∠BED = ∠ABE + ∠CDE (alternate angles). So ∠CDE = 80 − 35 = 45.

q.t: Interior angles on the same side of a transversal of two parallel lines are (2x + 15)° and (3x − 20)°. Find the smaller angle (in degrees).
A transversal cuts two parallel lines. The bisectors of a pair of alternate interior angles are:
q.e: The alternate angles are equal, so their halves are equal too — and those halves are alternate angles for the two bisectors, making the bisectors parallel.

q.t: In quadrilateral ABCD, AB ∥ DC. ∠A = 75° and ∠B = 110°. Find ∠C + ∠D (in degrees).
q.e: AD is a transversal: ∠A + ∠D = 180, so ∠D = 105. BC is a transversal: ∠B + ∠C = 180, so ∠C = 70. Sum 175.

q.t: A transversal makes co-interior angles of 95° and 85° with two lines. The lines are:
q.e: 95 + 85 = 180. If co-interior angles are supplementary, the lines are parallel — the rule works backwards too.

q.t: Two alternate interior angles on parallel lines add up to 136°. Find the co-interior partner of one of them (in degrees).
q.e: Alternate angles are equal, so each is 68°. Its co-interior partner is 180 − 68 = 112.

q.t: A transversal cuts two parallel lines. One angle is 3 times another angle that is NOT equal to it. Find the smaller angle (in degrees).
q.e: Only two sizes of angle appear, and they are supplementary. x + 3x = 180, so x = 45.

q.t: AB ∥ CD and P is a point between the lines. ∠BAP = 2x°, ∠PCD = 3x° and ∠APC = 100°. Find x.
q.e: A line through P parallel to both gives ∠APC = ∠BAP + ∠PCD: 2x + 3x = 100, so x = 20.

q.t: Three parallel lines p, q, r are cut by a transversal. An angle at p is 68°. The co-interior angle at q is a°, and the angle at r corresponding to a° is b°. Find b.
q.e: Co-interior with 68° gives a = 112. Corresponding angles on parallel lines are equal, so b = 112 too.

q.t: AB ∥ CD and E is a point between the lines. ∠ABE = 120° and ∠BED = 100°. Find ∠EDC (in degrees).
q.e: Line through E parallel to AB: the part of ∠BED next to B is 180 − 120 = 60°. The other part is 100 − 60 = 40°, co-interior with ∠EDC: 180 − 40 = 140.
